items.question: Across Joaquin Phoenix’s Oscar-night appearances connected to Joker, during which specific segment is his onstage moment actually underscored by the distinctly eerie orchestral Joker film score itself, rather than by more neutral, generic ceremony music?

options.A: When Joaquin Phoenix first walks out to accept his Actor in a Leading Role Oscar for Joker, as triumphant but stylistically neutral orchestral ceremony music swells beneath the standing ovation.
options.B: When Joaquin Phoenix is deep into his Actor in a Leading Role acceptance speech about animal rights and personal change, accompanied only by faint, unobtrusive orchestral underscore from the ceremony.
options.C: When the nominees for Actor in a Leading Role, including Joaquin Phoenix for Joker, are introduced over the montage and their names are read, with standard dramatic awards-show music playing in the background.
options.D: When the eerie string-led Joker cue plays under the on-screen credit for Hildur Guðnadóttir’s Original Score for Joker, just before she accepts her Oscar while Phoenix is only associated with the film offstage.

items.answer_text: When the eerie string-led Joker cue plays under the on-screen credit for Hildur Guðnadóttir’s Original Score for Joker, just before she accepts her Oscar while Phoenix is only associated with the film offstage.

trajectory_with_timestamps.reason: Identifying the distinctive eerie orchestral Joker score relies on the description of its sound, not visuals.

trajectory_with_timestamps.label: audio
trajectory_with_timestamps.reason: We must link the eerie Joker score cue to Hildur’s Oscar for Original Score for Joker, which is established via the spoken/winner announcement context.
